title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 1 Chronicles chapter 27 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 1 Chronicles Chapter 27.

questions.question: Who was the captain over the first course for the first month?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:2 states that Jashobeam the son of Zabdiel was over the first course for the first month.

questions.question: How many men were in each course throughout the months of the year?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:1 states that every course had twenty and four thousand men.

questions.question: Which tribe was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada associated with as a captain?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:5 refers to Benaiah the son of Jehoiada as a chief priest and captain but does not specify a tribe.

questions.question: Who was the captain over the fourth course for the fourth month?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:7 states Asahel the brother of Joab was the captain for the fourth month.

questions.question: True or False: Mikloth was the ruler in the course of Dodai an Ahohite.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:4 mentions Mikloth as the ruler in the course of Dodai an Ahohite.

questions.question: Which captain was mighty among the thirty and above the thirty?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:6 describes Benaiah as mighty among the thirty and above the thirty.

questions.question: Who was the captain over the seventh course for the seventh month?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:10 states Helez the Pelonite was the captain for the seventh month.

questions.question: Which captain was from the tribe of Benjamites?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:12 identifies Abiezer the Anetothite as of the Benjamites.

questions.question: True or False: The ruler of the Reubenites was Eliezer the son of Zichri.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:16 names Eliezer the son of Zichri as ruler of the Reubenites.

questions.question: Who was the ruler of the Simeonites?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:16 states Shephatiah the son of Maachah was ruler of the Simeonites.

questions.question: Who was over the vineyards according to 1 Chronicles 27?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:27 describes Shimei the Ramathite as over the vineyards.

questions.question: Who was the captain over the twelfth course for the twelfth month?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:15 states Heldai the Netophathite was captain for the twelfth month.

questions.question: True or False: David took a census of all Israelites from twenty years old and under.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:23 states David did not take the number of those twenty years old and under.

questions.question: Who was over the king's treasures?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:25 names Azmaveth the son of Adiel over the king's treasures.

questions.question: True or False: Joab was the general of the king's army.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:34 states Joab was the general of the king's army.

medium.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 1 Chronicles Chapter 27 to real-life situations.

questions.question: Who was the tenth captain for the tenth month, and what tribe was he from?
options: Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarhites
Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim
Helez the Pelonite, of the children of Ephraim
questions.correctAnswer: Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarhites
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:13 states that the tenth captain for the tenth month was Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarhites, and his course had twenty and four thousand men.

questions.question: What can we learn about leadership and responsibility from the list of tribal rulers in 1 Chronicles 27:16-22?
options: Each tribe had a designated ruler, showing organized stewardship and accountability
Only the Levites had rulers appointed, reflecting their special status
Rulers were chosen randomly without tribal association
Leadership was held only by priests and kings
questions.correctAnswer: Each tribe had a designated ruler, showing organized stewardship and accountability
questions.explanation: Verses 16-22 list rulers over each of the tribes of Israel, demonstrating that leadership was structured to ensure order and responsibility among the people.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 27:23, why did David not take the number of those twenty years old and under?
options: Because the LORD promised to increase Israel like the stars of the heavens
Because David was too busy with other matters
Because the people refused to be counted
Because Joab had already taken the count
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD promised to increase Israel like the stars of the heavens
questions.explanation: Verse 23 explains that David did not count those under twenty because God had promised to multiply Israel greatly, like the stars of the heavens.

questions.question: What happened when Joab began to number the people, according to 1 Chronicles 27:24?
options: He did not finish, because wrath fell against Israel
He finished successfully and recorded the numbers
He was praised for his obedience
He was promoted for his diligence
questions.correctAnswer: He did not finish, because wrath fell against Israel
questions.explanation: Verse 24 states that Joab started the numbering but did not finish because God's wrath fell upon Israel, and the number was not entered into David's chronicles.

questions.question: Who was appointed over the king's treasures in 1 Chronicles 27:25?
questions.explanation: Verse 25 clearly states that Azmaveth the son of Adiel was over the king's treasures.

questions.question: How does the appointment of different overseers for fields, vineyards, and herds in 1 Chronicles 27:26-31 teach about stewardship?
options: It shows that careful, specialized oversight is important for managing resources effectively
It suggests that only the king should manage resources directly
It implies that resources were unimportant to Israel's economy
It means that no one was responsible for the king's substance
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that careful, specialized oversight is important for managing resources effectively
questions.explanation: Verses 26-31 describe specific individuals overseeing different aspects of the king's property, indicating the importance of responsible stewardship and division of labor.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 27:18, Elihu was one of David's brothers and the ruler of the tribe of Judah.
questions.explanation: Verse 18 states that Elihu, one of David's brethren, was ruler of Judah, confirming the statement is true.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched as rulers over their respective tribes according to 1 Chronicles 27:20-21?
options: Hoshea son of Azaziah over Ephraim and Joel son of Pedaiah over half the tribe of Manasseh
Joel son of Pedaiah over Ephraim and Hoshea son of Azaziah over half the tribe of Manasseh
Iddo son of Zechariah over Ephraim and Jaasiel son of Abner over Benjamin
Omri son of Michael over Naphtali and Jerimoth son of Azriel over Issachar
questions.correctAnswer: Hoshea son of Azaziah over Ephraim and Joel son of Pedaiah over half the tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Verses 20-21 identify Hoshea son of Azaziah as ruler over Ephraim and Joel son of Pedaiah over half the tribe of Manasseh, correctly matching the pairs.

questions.question: What does 1 Chronicles 27:24 teach about obedience and the consequences of disobedience?
options: Joab's incomplete numbering led to wrath falling on Israel, showing that disobedience has serious consequences
Joab was rewarded for his initiative in numbering the people
The numbering was irrelevant to Israel's wellbeing
Disobedience was overlooked by the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: Joab's incomplete numbering led to wrath falling on Israel, showing that disobedience has serious consequences
questions.explanation: Verse 24 shows that Joab's counting angered God and was incomplete, teaching that disobedience or acting against God's will can bring judgment.

questions.question: Who was the general of King David's army according to 1 Chronicles 27:34?
questions.explanation: Verse 34 states that Joab was the general of the king's army, confirming his military leadership role.

questions.question: True or False: According to 1 Chronicles 27:32, Jonathan, David's uncle, was a counsellor, wise man, and scribe.
questions.explanation: Verse 32 confirms Jonathan, the king's uncle, served as a counsellor, wise man, and scribe, validating the statement as true.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 27:17, who were the rulers over the Levites and Aaronites?
options: Hashabiah the son of Kemuel over the Levites, and Zadok over the Aaronites
Shephatiah the son of Maachah over the Levites, and Eliezer the son of Zichri over the Aaronites
Jaasiel the son of Abner over the Levites, and Hoshea the son of Azaziah over the Aaronites
Joab over the Levites, and Ahithophel over the Aaronites
questions.correctAnswer: Hashabiah the son of Kemuel over the Levites, and Zadok over the Aaronites
questions.explanation: Verse 17 states that Hashabiah the son of Kemuel was ruler of the Levites, and Zadok was ruler of the Aaronites.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith and patience can be drawn from David's decision not to number those under twenty years old in 1 Chronicles 27:23, especially in light of God's promise?
options: Trusting God's promise means waiting patiently without relying solely on human measures
One should always rely on numbers and human strength
Counting people is unnecessary in all situations
God's promises relieve us of all responsibilities
questions.correctAnswer: Trusting God's promise means waiting patiently without relying solely on human measures
questions.explanation: David refrained from numbering the younger generation because he trusted God's promise to multiply Israel, teaching us to have faith and patience rather than depending only on human efforts (verse 23).

questions.question: Who was the eleventh captain for the eleventh month, and what tribe was he from according to 1 Chronicles 27:14?
options: Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim
Maharai the Netophathite, of the Zarhites
Abiezer the Anetothite, of the Benjamites
questions.correctAnswer: Benaiah the Pirathonite, of the children of Ephraim
questions.explanation: Verse 14 identifies Benaiah the Pirathonite from Ephraim as the captain for the eleventh month with twenty and four thousand men.

questions.question: True or False: 1 Chronicles 27:22 states that Azareel son of Jeroham was the prince of the tribe of Dan.
questions.explanation: Verse 22 explicitly names Azareel son of Jeroham as the prince of the tribe of Dan, confirming the statement.

hard.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 1 Chronicles Chapter 27.

questions.question: Who was over the king's treasures according to 1 Chronicles 27?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:25 states that Azmaveth the son of Adiel was over the king's treasures, indicating his responsibility for the royal finances.

questions.question: Which individual was responsible for overseeing the storehouses in the fields, cities, villages, and castles?
questions.explanation: Verse 25 of 1 Chronicles 27 assigns Jehonathan the son of Uzziah as the overseer of storehouses in various locations, showing his administrative role in supply management.

questions.question: Who was in charge of those who worked the fields for tillage of the ground?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 27:26, Ezri the son of Chelub was responsible for the workers who tilled the land, highlighting his role in agriculture.

questions.question: Which two men had roles connected to the vineyards and the increase of vineyards for wine cellars?
options: Shimei the Ramathite and Zabdi the Shiphmite
Obil the Ishmaelite and Jehdeiah the Meronothite
questions.correctAnswer: Shimei the Ramathite and Zabdi the Shiphmite
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:27 identifies Shimei as the overseer of vineyards and Zabdi as responsible for the increase of the vineyards related to wine cellars, showing specialized agricultural roles.

questions.question: Who was responsible over the olive trees and sycomore trees in the low plains?
questions.explanation: Verse 28 clearly states Baalhanan the Gederite was over the olive and sycomore trees in the low plains, indicating specific duties in horticulture.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs were responsible for overseeing herds, and in which geographical regions did they serve?
options: Shitrai the Sharonite in Sharon and Shaphat in the valleys
Obil the Ishmaelite in the low plains and Jaziz the Hagerite in Sharon
Jehdeiah the Meronothite in the fields and Joash in the vineyards
Azmaveth in the cities and Jehonathan in the castles
questions.correctAnswer: Shitrai the Sharonite in Sharon and Shaphat in the valleys
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:29 assigns Shitrai to the herds in Sharon and Shaphat the son of Adlai to herds in the valleys, demonstrating geographical division of responsibilities.

questions.question: Over which animal was Obil the Ishmaelite appointed?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:30 specifies that Obil the Ishmaelite was over the camels, indicating his role in managing these valuable animals.

questions.question: Who was the general of King David's army as stated in this chapter?
questions.explanation: According to 1 Chronicles 27:34, Joab was the general of the king's army, showing his military leadership under King David.

questions.question: Which counselor of King David is mentioned as a wise man and scribe who was also David's uncle?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:32 identifies Jonathan, David's uncle, as a counsellor, wise man, and scribe, highlighting his influential role in David's court.

questions.question: True or False: Ahithophel served as King David's companion.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:33 states Ahithophel was the king's counsellor, but Hushai the Archite was the king's companion, so Ahithophel was not the companion.

questions.question: True or False: Zabdi the Shiphmite was responsible for the increase of vineyards for the wine cellars.
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:27 clearly states Zabdi the Shiphmite was over the increase of the vineyards for the wine cellars, confirming his role.

questions.question: Which tribe's ruler was Eliezer the son of Zichri?
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:16 assigns Eliezer son of Zichri as ruler of the Reubenites, indicating his tribal leadership.

questions.question: The Hebrew word 'Ezri' in the name 'Ezri son of Chelub' can be associated with which meaning related to his role?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root of the name Ezri comes from 'ezer' meaning 'help' or 'support', fitting his role overseeing field workers (1 Chronicles 27:26) as a helper in agricultural tasks.

questions.question: Which literary device is evident in the listing of captains of the host in 1 Chronicles 27, where each month has a corresponding leader and equal number of men?
questions.explanation: The chapter employs parallelism by structuring each month's captain and their 24,000 men in a balanced, repetitive pattern (1 Chronicles 27:2-15), emphasizing order and completeness.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of God's promise to increase Israel 'like the stars of the heavens' as mentioned in this chapter?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11:12 references God's promise to Abraham that his offspring would be as numerous as the stars, paralleling 1 Chronicles 27:23's mention of God's promise to increase Israel similarly.

theological.title: 1 Chronicles Chapter 27 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 1 Chronicles Chapter 27 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's providence is demonstrated by the organization of Israel's military and administrative leaders as described in 1 Chronicles 27:1?
options: God sovereignly orders and governs the affairs of His people
God is distant and uninvolved in earthly matters
Human leaders are entirely independent from divine guidance
Military strength alone secures God's blessing
questions.correctAnswer: God sovereignly orders and governs the affairs of His people
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:1 shows a detailed, divinely ordered structure of leadership and service under the king, illustrating God's providential governance over Israel's affairs, consistent with passages like Psalm 103:19 and Proverbs 21:1.

questions.question: According to 1 Chronicles 27:5-6, how does Benaiah's role illustrate the doctrine of God equipping leaders for His purposes?
options: God raises mighty men above others to fulfill His plans
Leaders achieve might through personal ambition alone
Military leaders operate independently of God's will
All leaders have equal authority and power
questions.correctAnswer: God raises mighty men above others to fulfill His plans
questions.explanation: Verses 5-6 present Benaiah as 'mighty among the thirty, and above the thirty,' indicating God's sovereign choice and empowerment of leaders for His divine purposes, paralleling 2 Timothy 2:21 and Exodus 18:21.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed by the fact that David did not number those under twenty years old because the LORD promised to increase Israel as the stars of heaven (1 Chronicles 27:23)?
options: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.correctAnswer: God's faithfulness to His covenant promises
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:23 reflects God's faithfulness and mercy in fulfilling His promise to multiply Israel abundantly, echoing the covenant with Abraham (Genesis 15:5) and Psalm 89:34.

questions.question: How does the role of Joab beginning to number Israel but not finishing because of God's wrath (1 Chronicles 27:24) teach about sin and divine judgment?
options: Sin incurs God's judgment even on leaders
Sin is overlooked if done in service
God does not punish numbering of people
questions.correctAnswer: Sin incurs God's judgment even on leaders
questions.explanation: Verse 24 clearly indicates that counting the people was an act leading to divine wrath, demonstrating that even leaders are accountable for sin, consistent with Numbers 1:3 and 2 Samuel 24.

questions.question: What combined theological insight about God's sovereign distribution of roles and stewardship is taught by 1 Chronicles 27:25-31?
options: God ordains leaders over diverse stewardship tasks, reflecting His order and provision
Leadership roles are randomly assigned without divine purpose
Only military leadership matters to God
Economic tasks are less important to God than worship
questions.correctAnswer: God ordains leaders over diverse stewardship tasks, reflecting His order and provision
questions.explanation: Verses 25-31 detail leaders over treasures, fields, vineyards, flocks—indicating God's sovereign ordering of stewardship in all aspects of life, aligning with Genesis 2:15 and Colossians 1:16.

questions.question: From 1 Chronicles 27:16-22, what doctrinal truth about God's covenant people and tribal leadership is revealed?
options: God establishes tribal princes to administer His covenant community
Leadership in Israel was chaotic and unstructured
Tribal leaders were all from Judah only
God rejects tribal distinctions in leadership
questions.correctAnswer: God establishes tribal princes to administer His covenant community
questions.explanation: Verses 16-22 show appointed princes over each tribe, reflecting God's orderly governance of His covenant people, as also seen in Exodus 18:21 and Deuteronomy 1:13.

questions.question: How does the presence of Ahithophel as king's counsellor and Hushai as companion (1 Chronicles 27:33) contribute to understanding divine sovereignty in human counsel?
options: God uses human advisors for His purposes, even amidst conflicting counsel
Human counsel is always perfect and infallible
God is absent from political affairs
Counsellors act independently of divine will
questions.correctAnswer: God uses human advisors for His purposes, even amidst conflicting counsel
questions.explanation: 1 Chronicles 27:33 highlights contrasting advisors, showing God's sovereignty over human counsel, consistent with Proverbs 15:22 and Daniel 2:21.

questions.question: What synthesis can be drawn from 1 Chronicles 27:1 and 1 Chronicles 27:32 regarding the integration of leadership and wisdom in David's administration?
options: God combines military, administrative, and wise counsel to establish a well-ordered kingdom
Military leaders held all power without counsel
Wisdom was irrelevant to David's rule
questions.correctAnswer: God combines military, administrative, and wise counsel to establish a well-ordered kingdom
questions.explanation: Verse 1 shows organized courses with captains; verse 32 depicts wise counsellors like Jonathan and Jehiel, indicating God's orchestration of comprehensive leadership for His kingdom, paralleling Proverbs 11:14 and 1 Kings 4:29-34.

questions.question: What does the appointment of Jehoiada, Abiathar, and Joab as king's counsellors and general (1 Chronicles 27:34) teach about God's providence in leadership?
options: God appoints leaders with different roles to fulfill His purposes
Leadership roles were assigned by popular vote
Only priests held authority in Israel
Military and spiritual leadership never overlap
questions.correctAnswer: God appoints leaders with different roles to fulfill His purposes
questions.explanation: Verse 34 shows a division of authority—counsellors and general—demonstrating God's providential appointment of various leaders to implement His will, consistent with Romans 13:1 and Exodus 24:13-14.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that detailed military and administrative records in 1 Chronicles 27:1-15 are mere human inventions with no divine significance. What does 1 Chronicles 27:1-15 actually teach about God's involvement in Israel's leadership?
options: It teaches that God sovereignly ordains and sustains leadership structures for His covenant promises
It shows that human organization is independent of God
It suggests God is uninvolved in Israel's military affairs
It promotes human pride in military power
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that God sovereignly ordains and sustains leadership structures for His covenant promises
questions.explanation: Verses 1-15 present a divinely ordered military rotation, showing God's providential involvement, consistent with Psalm 75:6-7 and Daniel 4:17.

questions.question: What does the command not to number those under twenty (1 Chronicles 27:23) reveal about God's attribute of mercy within covenantal relationship?
options: God mercifully withholds judgment and promises growth
God is indifferent to Israel's population
God's mercy is unrelated to census practices
God punishes all counting of people
questions.correctAnswer: God mercifully withholds judgment and promises growth
questions.explanation: Verse 23 reflects God's mercy by preventing a census that might lead to judgment, instead promising increase, aligning with Exodus 33:19 and Lamentations 3:22-23.

questions.question: How do the tribal leaders listed in 1 Chronicles 27:16-22 foreshadow the New Testament concept of the unity and diversity in the body of Christ?
options: Different leaders serve distinct tribes yet form one nation, paralleling diverse members unified in Christ
Leadership was uniform with no diversity
questions.correctAnswer: Different leaders serve distinct tribes yet form one nation, paralleling diverse members unified in Christ
questions.explanation: Verses 16-22 show varied leaders over tribes within one Israel, reflecting 1 Corinthians 12:12-27 where believers have diverse gifts but form one body.

questions.question: What theological significance does the presence of Zadok the Aaronite as a tribal ruler (1 Chronicles 27:17) have regarding the priesthood and kingship relationship?
options: It illustrates the interrelation of priestly authority with Israel's civil governance
Priests had no role beyond worship
Kingship and priesthood were entirely separate
questions.correctAnswer: It illustrates the interrelation of priestly authority with Israel's civil governance
questions.explanation: Verse 17 names Zadok, a priestly line, as ruler, showing priestly involvement in governance, consistent with Exodus 28 and Hebrews 7.

questions.question: What synthesis about God's justice and mercy can be derived from 1 Chronicles 27:24 and 1 Chronicles 27:23 together?
options: God balances judgment for sin with covenantal promises of mercy and growth
questions.correctAnswer: God balances judgment for sin with covenantal promises of mercy and growth
questions.explanation: Verse 24 shows wrath for numbering (judgment), while verse 23 shows mercy in not numbering young men and promising increase. This balance reflects God's just yet merciful nature, as in Exodus 34:6-7 and Romans 11:22.

questions.question: How does the detailed record of leaders over agricultural and economic resources (1 Chronicles 27:26-31) reveal God's attribute of providence?
options: God providentially oversees and sustains all aspects of creation and human economy
God is concerned only with spiritual matters
Economic details are irrelevant to divine providence
questions.correctAnswer: God providentially oversees and sustains all aspects of creation and human economy
questions.explanation: Verses 26-31 assign leadership over fields, vineyards, trees, and animals, reflecting God's providential care over all creation, as supported by Matthew 6:26 and Colossians 1:17.
